findings.title: A blocking check that fails in two LLM-owned sections is repaired in only the first of them: validation_defects collapses the failure set to named[0], so the second section is never attempted and the one-attempt rule then closes the transaction
findings.detail: BC-08 failed with three failures this draw: inherited_unit:026.paragraph and inherited_unit:028.paragraph (both VERIFIED_REWRITE) in section additional_examples, and inherited_unit:111.code_block (CORRECT_WITH_EVIDENCE) in section development_testing - each of them 'keeps the command cmake --build build but the candidate does not render it'. validation_defects builds ONE Defect per failing check and sets its section to `named[0] if named else None`, so the whole check is routed to additional_examples and repair_packet hands the model that section's stage_output alone. No revision of additional_examples can make development_testing render anything, so that third failure is structurally unrepairable in the round; the next validation then sees the equivalent failure standing and the transaction fails closed. Replayed mechanically through the production function on this run's own artifacts: llm_sections is the 9 authored sections including development_testing, validation_defects returns exactly 1 defect, section_id 'additional_examples', carrying all three failures in its record but able to revise only one section's output. Fix: one repairable defect per failing (check, LLM-owned section) pair, so each named section gets its own attempt under its own fingerprint, rather than one defect whose record names sections it cannot reach. Mutation test: this validation.json and these 9 sections - red (one defect, development_testing never attempted) before, green (two defects, one per named section) after. Alternative rejected: widening the single repair packet to carry every named section's output, which asks one reply to revise several stages' artifacts at once and loses repair_checks' per-section binding - the RC1 failure family the packet's narrowing was written to stop.
findings.evidence: validation.json BC-08 failures (three, across additional_examples and development_testing); repairs.json - a single attempt, section_id additional_examples, on both draws; offline replay of validation_defects over this run's validation.json and content_units.json.

findings.title: A BC-08 protected-content repair is asked to restore text whose only SUPPORTED fact is an inherited_unit - the one kind repair_packet strips out of the facts it may cite
findings.detail: BC-08's entire subject is a protected inherited_unit's own text. repair_packet builds its fact records as `kinds = [kind for kind in FACT_KINDS if kind != 'inherited_unit']`, so the packet for a BC-08 repair contains every kind EXCEPT the one the defect is about. Measured on this repository: exactly four facts carry the string 'cmake --build build' and all four are inherited_unit (018.code_block SUPERSEDE_REDUNDANT, 026.paragraph, 028.paragraph, 111.code_block); install_command:cmake's own value stops at 'git clone ... && cd ... && cmake -S . -B build', the configure step, which is exactly what the candidate does render (README line 67). The repair is therefore asked to add a command for which no citable SUPPORTED fact is in its packet, while BC-04 requires every content unit to cite existing SUPPORTED facts. The model's answer was the same both times: it returned the targeted unit unchanged (before == after, 'Encrypt a document using AES-256 with user and owner passwords.'), outcome 'repaired', BC-08 re-raised. That is a no-op measured twice under two different prompts and two different request hashes - a533743c under targeted_repair 8 and 85353fed under targeted_repair 9, each a live call - so it is a property of the packet, not a draw. Fix: include the defect's own protected inherited_unit records in a BC-08 repair packet, since they are SUPPORTED facts the candidate is required to preserve, and the exclusion exists to stop a repair citing the corpus it was not authoring, not to hide the evidence the defect names. Mutation test: this defect and these facts - red (packet holds no fact carrying 'cmake --build build') before, green (the three named inherited_unit records present) after. Alternative rejected: letting BC-08 accept a paraphrase without a citation, which weakens a blocking check and is prohibited.
findings.evidence: facts.json - the four facts containing 'cmake --build build', all kind inherited_unit; install_command:cmake's value; repairs.json attempts a533743c (prompt 8) and 85353fed (prompt 9), both before == after; calls.jsonl S11 targeted_repair rows, 2 of them, both live.

findings.title: A prompt-version bump isolated to one call: the same transaction replayed across a rebase produced byte-identical bytes for one provider call
findings.detail: The first draw ran on 23a8905 (REVIEWER_LOGIC_VERSION 4, targeted_repair prompt 8): 49 ledger rows, 26 provider calls, 23 cache reuses, 1 response_invalid, 52,980 completion tokens. The reviewer's mid-run message then reported arrival item 64 landed at 846eaaf, and the worktree was rebased onto it. The identical `present` invocation on the rebased tree produced 47 further rows of which 46 were cache_reuse and exactly ONE was a live call - the targeted_repair under prompt 9, 1,469 completion tokens - because the prompt change moved that one request's hash and nothing else's. Every artifact digest was unchanged: source d2b6a656..., facts bd8f4a98..., dispositions db09fe4a..., plan e035dee1..., content_units 33c62e26..., README 5fa7f2ee..., validation e6c39d54.... Two things follow. First, the call store's reuse is exact and prompt-addressed, not approximate: 96 rows across two draws with zero cache_stale, on a second transaction independent of run 3's. Second, the repair no-op of finding F2 is reproducible across a prompt revision, which is what makes it a packet property rather than one unlucky reply.
findings.evidence: calls.jsonl rows 1-49 and 50-96; both runs' stdout digests; prompts/targeted_repair.yaml version 8 at 23a8905 and 9 at 846eaaf.

Draw 3: BC-01..BC-09 PASS after one BC-08 repair, BC-10 FAIL (F06, F10). Draw 4, this run: BC-08 FAIL, BC-10 never judged. The honest reading is that this candidate's blocker is not one defect but a sequence of them, each drawn: BC-02, then BC-10 twice, now BC-08. findings.title: PDF C++ is not drawn a fifth time in this box, and the candidate is not forced
findings.detail: The transaction is byte-reproducible from its call store, so a re-run cannot change the outcome; the only way to a different draw is to clear the store and re-roll the composition. Draw 3's own decision entry already ruled that re-rolling until a check says yes is what the W-card's stop-don't-force forbids, and it forbids it more firmly now that reuse has made a re-roll cheap. The two causes are named mechanically above and both are shared code this lane may not edit. Nothing here weakens BC-08: the check is right - the candidate genuinely omits a build command three protected inherited units keep, and the upstream README carries it, so it is a real gap under loop-prompt rule 8, not a false positive. Alternative rejected: deleting runs/transactions/.../calls and drawing again, which would spend ~26 live calls on a coin flip whose odds are 1 of 2 by the four-draw record above.
findings.evidence: This run's validation.json (BC-08 FAIL, BC-10 PENDING), reported literally; the byte-identical second draw.
